properties.description:
ARRIVED 2026-09-12. The launch path stopped serving target/debug and now serves a release-profile binary, rebuilt on the builder's word rather than on every launch. First of the four Anthony ordered on 2026-09-11 ("go with your suggested order").

WHY IT WAS FIRST: no design work stood in front of it, and it was the largest measured user-visible win on the board — a propagate walk 5,851 ms → 62 ms warm (93x), design_regions 12.5 s → 2.0 s warm, same bytes and same path with only the profile changed. Every performance number in the 2026-09-10/11 sweep was taken on the debug binary, so nothing else in that backlog could be judged until this landed.

THE INCREMENT'S OWN QUESTION — how the wrapper decides "deliberately" — WAS ANSWERED: it does not decide. The launcher never builds in release mode. A missing binary is a refusal that names `tools/reflow2-rebuild.sh`; a binary older than the source is served behind an unconditional banner naming both hashes; and `REFLOW2_PROFILE=debug` restores the previous content-hash auto-rebuild for the edit-compile loop, unchanged.

THE HAZARD THE TRADE REINTRODUCED, AND WHAT ANSWERS IT: the auto-rebuild existed because a stale binary served stale VOCABULARY in silence (2026-08-16, the pre-#199 change_type enum). Not rebuilding brings that back, so the banner is unconditional and `tools/launch_serves_release.py` fails the build if the staleness comparison is ever removed. That gate was SHOWN TO FAIL on two injected regressions before it was trusted.

WHAT IT DID NOT INCLUDE, as planned: the adjacency memo work. 142 edge-read call sites still go to the store against 1 using the index built in #479, unattributed as a share of the seconds. Keeping it out is what leaves the profile's contribution measurable.

MEASURED ON THE WAY OUT: the deliberate rebuild took 7m28s warm, RocksDB already compiled. The ~34-minute figure in the plan is the cold case and remains the reason this is not automatic.

NO VERSION NUMBER BY DESIGN (dec:idea-a-planned-increment-is-named-by-content-not-by-number).
properties.name: A session serves a release binary
